evals.name: percentual-vo
evals.prompt: cria o value object Percentual pro rateio de frete — tem que ficar entre 0 e 100, com duas casas decimais
evals.expected_output: A percentual.vo.ts value object: private constructor, static create returning Result with a named DomainError for out-of-range/precision, immutable, behavior on the VO.
assertions: File follows kebab-case + type suffix naming (percentual.vo.ts)
Constructor is private and performs no validation
A static create factory returns a Result (or equivalent) instead of throwing for rule refusals
The 0-100 range and two-decimal precision are validated with named, greppable error codes
The VO is immutable (readonly state; operations return new instances)

evals.name: assinatura-relogio-rolante-legado
evals.prompt: modela o agregado Assinatura com Plano: renovar usa relógio rolante — renovar antes do fim não encurta o período pago — e assinatura cancelada não renova. o banco é legado e tem datas inválidas, preciso conseguir ler e corrigir
evals.expected_output: An assinatura.aggregate.ts with private constructor, validating create, lenient restore (legacy mode) paired with a validating save/violations mechanism, typed ids, renew(now) taking time as argument, rolling-clock anchoring on the previous period end, canceled-cannot-renew as a named DomainError.
assertions: Aggregate has a private constructor plus static create (validates) and static restore
restore is lenient (no birth validation) BECAUSE the database is legacy - and something holds the line on write (violations()/validating save)
Time enters as an argument (renew(now) or injected clock), never Date.now() inside the rule
Rolling clock: the new period anchors on the previous end when renewing early
A canceled subscription refuses renewal via a named domain error, not a throw
Ids are typed per aggregate (not raw strings everywhere)

evals.name: credito-atomico-money
evals.prompt: adiciona a regra de crédito na Organizacao: débito atômico antes de qualquer chamada de IA, saldo nunca pode ficar negativo, tudo em centavos
evals.expected_output: A debit rule living ON the Organizacao aggregate (a named method guarding the invariant), money as integer cents (Money VO or equivalent), insufficient-balance refused via Result + named DomainError, no float arithmetic.
assertions: The debit rule is a method ON the aggregate, not a loose function or anemic service
Money is integer minor units (cents); no float arithmetic on amounts
A debit that would go negative is refused via Result with a named error code, not a throw
No public setters - state changes only through the rule-guarding method

evals.name: listagem-query-read-model
evals.prompt: cria a listagem de assinaturas ativas com o nome do plano e o fim do período — não quero carregar agregado pra isso
evals.expected_output: A query in application/queries going straight to the database (ORM/client inline), returning its own read model interface shaped for the screen; no repository, no aggregate loading, no writes.
assertions: The read path is a query (application/queries), not a repository returning aggregates
The query returns its own read model type - not an ORM row type, not a domain aggregate
The query performs no insert/update/delete
The join/projection happens in the database call, not by loading aggregates and mapping in memory

evals.name: erro-certo-canal-certo
evals.prompt: no handler de renovar assinatura eu devolvo DomainError('subscription.not-found') quando não acha, e no repositório eu devolvo Result.fail(DomainError('persistence-failed')) quando o supabase dá erro. tá certo isso?
evals.expected_output: A review that says both are the wrong type: not-found is an ApplicationError (the handler, not the aggregate, produces it - returned in Result, signature becomes Result<void, UseCaseError>); the Supabase failure is an InfrastructureError THROWN from the repository with the driver error as `cause`, never returned - the handler has nothing to route on, the global filter answers 503. Explains the mechanism (who routes on it) rather than citing layers.
assertions: not-found is reclassified as an ApplicationError returned in Result, not a DomainError
The handler's return type becomes Result<void, UseCaseError> (DomainError | ApplicationError), not DomainError alone
The Supabase failure is turned into a thrown InfrastructureError, not a Result.fail
The InfrastructureError wraps the driver error as `cause` and carries a stable code
The explanation is based on who routes on the error (the handler cannot route on a db outage), not on 'it came from layer X'
No try/catch is added to the handler for the infrastructure failure
